title: Provider-neutral tracker seam and the GitHub adapter
summary: Adds a provider-neutral `Tracker` seam to the osf crate — a trait, its data types, a ready rule, a finishing-write helper, and an in-memory test double — plus the first adapter, `GitHubTracker`, which drives GitHub Issues and Projects v2 through the installed `gh` CLI. Every adapter request is one `gh` invocation whose argv and JSON payload are built by pure functions and whose response is read by a pure parser, so the adapter is a thin loop over a `GhRunner`. The seam itself names no provider; a test enforces that only `github_tracker.rs` may mention GitHub.

nodes.label: Engine run
nodes.subtitle: pick → capabilities → writes
nodes.summary: The caller's use of the seam: pick one dispatchable item, require the capabilities the run needs, then write state and recap. Exercised end to end by tests/tracker_fake_run.rs.

nodes.label: Tracker trait
nodes.subtitle: read_ready / write_state / write_recap / capabilities
nodes.summary: The seam between the factory and a work tracker. Object-safe; an adapter must not filter by the ready status itself, and a blocked write records the cause before moving the status.

nodes.label: Tracker data types
nodes.subtitle: WorkItem, WorkItemId, WorkState, Capability
nodes.summary: Provider-neutral value types: WorkItemId parses and displays as provider:repo#item, WorkState and BlockedCause serialize to pinned kebab-case names, and Capability states what a tracker can do rather than assuming it.

nodes.label: Ready rule
nodes.subtitle: dispatchable / pick
nodes.summary: Decides which read items the engine may dispatch: open, status ready, every blocker closed. Kept out of every adapter so the rule is provider-neutral.

nodes.label: Finishing writes
nodes.subtitle: require_capabilities / finish_run
nodes.summary: Checks the needed states and the recap against the tracker's reported capabilities, then writes the state and the recap, stopping at the first failure and naming the step.

nodes.label: FakeTracker
nodes.subtitle: in-memory double, records every call
nodes.summary: An in-memory Tracker that records every call as plain data and does no I/O. Scriptable reads, capabilities, and per-operation or per-state failures.

nodes.label: GitHubTracker
nodes.subtitle: Tracker over GitHub Issues + Projects v2
nodes.summary: The first adapter. read_ready verifies the configured status field, then pages project items; write_state resolves the project, the item id and the option, posts a cause comment for a blocked state, then runs the mutation.

nodes.label: GhRunner
nodes.subtitle: run(argv, stdin) -> stdout
nodes.summary: The one side-effecting seam of the adapter: runs one gh invocation and returns stdout, trimmed stderr on a non-zero exit, or a cannot-run error. RealGhRunner spawns the program with a 60-second default timeout.

nodes.label: argv and payload builders
nodes.subtitle: read_ready_payload, mutation_payload, comment_argv, …
nodes.summary: Pure functions that build the argv and the JSON body of every request: the ready-items page, the project status query, the item-id query, the field mutation, and the comment POST.

nodes.label: response parsers
nodes.subtitle: parse_items_page, parse_project_status, parse_item_id, parse_write_result
nodes.summary: Pure parsers for every response. A malformed item that is not in the ready status is kept as a skipped item whose status begins with unreadable:, so one bad non-ready item does not fail the page.

nodes.label: gh CLI
nodes.subtitle: installed command-line tool
nodes.summary: The installed gh program. Every adapter request is one invocation of it, with the GraphQL body fed on standard input.

nodes.label: GitHub GraphQL API
nodes.subtitle: Issues and Projects v2
nodes.summary: The remote API gh calls: project items with their status field, issue blockers, project item ids, and the updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue mutation.

nodes.label: Provider-neutrality test
nodes.subtitle: tracker_neutral.rs
nodes.summary: Walks crates/osf/src/tracker and fails if any file names a provider or tool, splitting camel-case tokens so GHRunner counts as gh. It also asserts the folder holds exactly its four files.

edges.label: pick / finish_run
edges.summary: The engine's whole use of the seam: pick one dispatchable item, then finish the run through the trait.
The trait's signatures are built from the provider-neutral value types.

edges.label: read_ready
edges.summary: pick reads through the trait and applies the dispatchable rule to what comes back.

edges.label: capabilities, write_state, write_recap
edges.summary: finish_run checks capabilities, then writes the state and the recap through the trait.

edges.label: impl Tracker
edges.summary: The double implements the seam and records every call as plain data.

edges.label: impl Tracker
edges.summary: The first adapter implements the seam; the trait stays provider-neutral while this file carries the GitHub specifics.

edges.label: run(argv, stdin)
edges.summary: Every request the adapter makes goes through the runner, which is the only side-effecting seam.
The adapter builds each request's argv and JSON body with the pure builders.
The adapter reads each response with the pure parsers.

edges.label: spawn, stdin, timeout
edges.summary: RealGhRunner spawns the program, feeds the payload on standard input, drains both pipes on their own threads, and kills it after the timeout.

edges.label: GraphQL over HTTPS
edges.summary: gh carries the GraphQL query or mutation to the GitHub API and returns the JSON response on standard output.

edges.label: no provider names
edges.summary: The test fails if any file under src/tracker names a provider or tool, keeping the seam neutral.

flows.title: read_ready: verify the field, then page the ready items
flows.summary: One read verifies the configured status field before any item page, then pages project items until the cursor runs out, parsing each page into work items.

messages.label: project status query
messages.note: One extra project query verifies the configured status field before any item page.

messages.label: project JSON
messages.note: parse_project_status reads the project id, the status field id and its options; a missing field makes the whole read Unknown.

messages.label: items page, cursor, skip query
messages.note: The skip query leaves the configured skip status out on the server; the loop stops after 50 pages or a repeated cursor.

messages.label: items page JSON
messages.note: parse_items_page keeps a malformed non-ready item as a skipped item whose status begins with unreadable:, and fails only on a malformed ready item.

flows.title: write_state: resolve, comment the cause, then mutate
flows.summary: A state write resolves the project and the item id, posts a cause comment when the state is blocked, and only then runs the single-select mutation.

messages.label: project status query
messages.note: The option name for the state is looked up in the project's options before anything is written.

messages.label: item id query
messages.note: The issue's project item id is read from its projectItems, matching the project id.

messages.label: POST comment: Blocked: <cause>.
messages.note: Only a blocked state posts a cause comment, and it is posted before the status moves so a blocked item always carries its cause.

messages.label: Ok / Rejected / Failed
messages.note: parse_write_result accepts only a response that names the written project item.
